problem: The extract gives this text, and the caucus sentence that f:incits-caucus quotes, under one heading, "INCITS Organization, Policies and Procedures (Version 2026.08.01), 7.17.1.3 and 7.17.1.4", without marking which subclause holds which sentence, so the extract cannot confirm 7.17.1.3 alone.
fix: Cite "(INCITS Organization, Policies and Procedures, 7.17.1.3 and 7.17.1.4)", or confirm the split in the INCITS source and mark it in the extract. f:incits-caucus, outside this scope, has the same problem with 7.17.1.4.

problem: ISO gives national bodies votes on enquiry and final drafts: "all National Bodies, irrespective of their status within a committee, have the right to vote on enquiry drafts (see 2.6) and on final draft International Standards (see 2.7)" (1.7). SD-4's working drafts are updated and adopted by plenary at every meeting ("Working draft handling") and reach national bodies only when sent for ballot, so "national bodies vote on each draft" says more than the text does.
fix: "and national bodies vote on each balloted draft as a whole" (p:checks already says "each balloted draft").

problem: SD-4 gives time-boxing only in its notes on the design subgroups ("The design subgroups (EWG and LEWG) own ... Notes:"), where "the chair might time-box initial discussion and then poll whether the subgroup is interested in discussing the proposal's details further." The sentence's other moves are given to subgroup chairs generally: "The subgroup chair may take any polls they choose", "Subgroup chairs prioritize first papers...", "subgroup chairs have discretion to allow limited exploration of alternatives", and Against voters "may be asked for their reasons by the chair".
fix: Move "time-box a new proposal" into the second sentence as a design room chair's move, or cite text that gives it to every chair.

problem: ISO 5.5 has the Secretary/Committee Manager or Project Leader/Convenor "ensure that meeting outcomes are properly documented and shared" and address comments on the minutes; it says nothing about how much of an argument minutes keep. SD-4 puts the writing with participants: "If you are present at a meeting of WG21 or any of its study groups, you should be prepared to take minutes, and to accept nomination to do so in the absence of volunteers."
fix: "So what minutes keep of an objection's argument rests first with whoever takes them, which SD-4 asks any participant present to be ready to do, and then with that officer, ..." and add SD-4's minute-taking sentence to f:minutes.

problem: SD-4 says "The proposal author is expected to participate in the design subgroup to present the proposal, answer questions, participate in design discussion, and implement any changes directed by the group." It says nothing about an author's record; that idea comes from ax:repeat, not from SD-4.
fix: "SD-4 expects an author to respond to review by taking part: presenting the proposal, answering questions, and making the changes the room directs." (the wording of l:review-needs-part).

problem: SD-4 sets the 5pm deadline only for the email lists ("in no case any later than the deadline of 5pm the evening before the closing plenary session"). For the national body it says only that the objector "should proactively raise it during the week", including "Within your own national body", with no clock time. The sentence puts both steps under the 5pm deadline.
fix: "SD-4 says objections not escalated during the week, on the email lists by 5pm the evening before plenary and within a national body, should get no weight there." p:late-objection, outside this scope, has the same wording.

problem: SD-4 asks one kind of paper for its known problems: "The TS or white paper should list known specific questions on which feedback is desired, including:" "What are the exit criteria (especially, the list of must-address controversial issues) before we can consider merging this TS or white paper into the IS?", and its goals section is to say how "firm" the design is so users can "estimate the degree of risk incurred using an implementation". f:no-drawbacks-asked confirms the absence only for proposal papers.
fix: "but it asks no proposal paper to state its design's drawbacks, and a paper is considered without them."

problem: ISO does more with final-draft comments than note them. 2.7.5 records them as "noted for future consideration" but adds that the Secretary/Committee Manager and the Office of the CEO "may seek to resolve obvious editorial errors", and 2.7.7 sends a failed final draft back "for reconsideration in light of the technical reasons submitted in support of the negative votes." Neither is a written answer.
fix: "On a final draft it records comments as noted for future consideration and requires no written answer to them."

problem: SD-4: "The design subgroups (EWG and LEWG) own selecting and recommending feature designs and ship vehicles (TS or IS)." An author can only ask for a vehicle (m:moves-author), so "choosing the IS" gives the author a move the rules give the design room.
fix: "and asking the design room for the IS where it can pass" (the phrasing of l:seeking-other-moves).

problem: As for p:disclosure: SD-4 asks a TS or white paper to list, among its exit criteria, "the list of must-address controversial issues" and to say how "firm" its design is; the confirmed absence covers proposal papers only.
fix: "since SD-4 asks no proposal paper to state its design's drawbacks and a paper is considered without them."

problem: SD-4 gives time-boxing a new proposal only in its notes on the design subgroups (EWG and LEWG). Ordering the agenda, limited exploration, re-polls, and asking Against voters for reasons are given to subgroup chairs generally.
fix: Drop "time-boxing a new proposal" and f:timebox from the basis, or cite text that gives the move to study group chairs.

problem: SD-4 gives the design subgroups ownership of "selecting and recommending feature designs and ship vehicles (TS or IS)"; an author can only ask for one, so "chooses the IS where it can pass" gives the author the design room's move.
fix: "and asks the design room for the IS where it can pass".

problem: In "national bodies ballot each draft": ISO gives national bodies votes on enquiry and final drafts (1.7, 2.6.3, 2.7.3), and the working drafts SD-4 has plenary adopt at every meeting go to national bodies only when sent for ballot.
fix: "and national bodies vote on each balloted draft" (as p:checks and inf:thm-checks say).

problem: As for p:disclosure: the confirmed absence covers proposal papers only, and SD-4 asks a TS or white paper to list its must-address controversial issues and say how "firm" its design is.
fix: "since SD-4 asks no proposal paper to state its drawbacks and considers a paper without them."

problem: Same text as the second thm:settled finding: national bodies vote on enquiry and final drafts (1.7, 2.6.3, 2.7.3), not on every working draft plenary adopts.
fix: "and national bodies vote on each balloted draft" (as inf:thm-checks says).

problem: SD-4 asks papers to take up more than alternatives and declined directions: the presenter "will personally produce a new revision of the paper based on feedback or else will communicate feedback to the author to do so", and the author is to "implement any changes directed by the group". What SD-4 does not ask is that a paper state the objections raised against it (f:no-paper-objections).
fix: "since SD-4 asks them to state no objection beyond showing the alternatives considered and defending a declined change."

problem: "Other things equal, each participant, sponsor, national body, and user prefers whatever brings it more of what it values, sooner and at less cost to it, weighing gains against losses on one scale of its own." (36 words) and "For this proof, a participant values adoption of the proposals they support, ... and their own time and money." (104 words)
fix: Other things equal, each participant, sponsor, national body, and user prefers more of what it values, sooner and cheaper, weighing gains against losses on one scale of its own. Then one sub-item per role: "A participant values adoption of proposals they support, their sponsor's interests, their standing, keeping any post they hold, their time and money, and a good result for users." "A sponsor values its interests, which can depend on particular features of a design." "A national body values the outcomes its national position supports, the interests concerned at its national level where it has no position yet, and its members' time." "A user values the features they use or would use, how well those features work, and their own time and money."

problem: "A chair cannot rule out that a consensus call not following the 2:1 norm, or polling that departs from what SD-4 encourages, puts their post at more risk than following them." (31 words)
fix: A chair cannot rule out that a consensus call departing from the 2:1 norm, or polling departing from what SD-4 encourages, puts their post at more risk than following them.

problem: "Reversing a decision, or changing a design after work is built on it, means redoing or discarding that work, which costs those who built it and takes meeting time from other papers." (32 words)
fix: Reversing a decision, or changing a design after work is built on it, means redoing or discarding that work, which costs its builders and takes meeting time from other papers.

problem: "each with the features approved by its cutoff"
fix: WG21 plans an edition of the C++ standard every three years, each with the features approved by its feature cutoff, and ISO publishes each once national bodies approve it.

problem: "A player does better with one option than another when it is worth more to them, by their weighing of the values a statement names, and does best with an option when no other is worth more." (37 words)
fix: A player does better with the option worth more to them, by their weighing of the values a statement names, and does best with one no other option exceeds.

problem: "With Neutral votes short of a majority of those voting, a chair follows the 2:1 norm by declaring consensus on a count above 2:1 after discussion and any re-poll, and on no other count." (34 words)
fix: With Neutral votes short of a majority of those voting, a chair follows the 2:1 norm by declaring consensus exactly on counts above 2:1 after discussion and any re-poll.

problem: "None of the ISO/IEC Directives Part 1 clauses listed here requires a written answer to an objection raised in a working group or on a ballot, apart from 2.6.5's requirement to respond to all comments received" (36 words before the source)
fix: Apart from 2.6.5's requirement to respond to all comments received, no ISO/IEC Directives Part 1 clause listed here requires a written answer to a working group or ballot objection (source and search terms unchanged).

problem: "The proof takes as given SD-4's text, who is convenor, the choices of wording room chairs, guests, participants who are not regulars, and the direction group, and the convenor's appointments, study groups, and guest invitations." (35 words)
fix: The proof takes as given SD-4's text, the convenor's identity, appointments, study groups, and guest invitations, and the choices of wording room chairs, guests, non-regular participants, and the direction group.

problem: "Design and wording room chairs call consensus to forward proposals, design room chairs can delay one a meeting for a paperless rival, and study group chairs can poll which design to send on." (33 words)
fix: Design and wording room chairs call consensus to forward proposals; design room chairs can delay one a meeting for a paperless rival; study group chairs can poll which design advances.

problem: "It can also object in SC22 and JTC 1 to action taken on a topic not on the agenda, and, together with at least one other P-member, have a draft discussed at a meeting when they disagree with the SC22 chair's decision on it." (44 words)
fix: A national body can appoint experts, vote Yes, No, or abstain on ballots, comment, state national positions in plenary, appeal, and object in SC22 and JTC 1 to off-agenda action. Together with at least one other P-member, it can also have a draft discussed at a meeting when they disagree with the SC22 chair's decision on it.

problem: "One Against vote changes the result only at one or two votes above the line"
fix: One Against vote changes the result only at one or two votes above the 2:1 threshold, and at least a third of Favor-plus-Against votes cast Against keeps the norm unmet.

problem: "though SD-4 says a Neutral majority of those voting can be concerning" (the claim holds without the concession)
fix: The 2:1 comparison counts only Favor and Against votes, and SD-4 says a Neutral majority of those voting can be concerning.

problem: "It risks the colleague's later support no less"
fix: It risks the colleague's later support at least as much, and SD-4 tells only Against voters to be ready to give reasons, which take time to prepare.

problem: "only when the count sits one or two votes above the line, though it can also win changes to the design"
fix: One Against vote changes the result only when the count is one or two votes above the 2:1 threshold, and it can also bring changes to the design.

problem: "A participant can argue for another design and still vote Neutral, which leaves the count unchanged and, unlike Against, is a vote SD-4 asks no one to be ready to explain." (31 words)
fix: A participant can argue for another design yet vote Neutral, which leaves the count unchanged and, unlike Against, is a vote SD-4 asks no one to be ready to explain.

problem: "When each one's doubt is worth less than that risk and the time for reasons, each does better refraining whatever the other does, and both do better than if both opposed." (31 words)
fix: If each one's doubt is worth less than that risk and the time for reasons, each does better refraining whatever the other does, and both do better than both opposing.

problem: "A proposal can advance through WG21 with objections unresolved, since it needs consensus calls, under the 2:1 norm in the rooms and by the convenor at plenary, not every objector's persuasion." (31 words; "the rooms" also stands in for subgroups)
fix: A proposal can advance through WG21 with objections unresolved, since it needs consensus calls, under the 2:1 norm in subgroups and by the convenor at plenary, not every objector's persuasion.

problem: "A proposal can advance while discussed objections to it remain unresolved, because it advances on consensus calls, under the 2:1 norm in the rooms and by the convenor at plenary, and consensus need not imply unanimity." (36 words; "the rooms" also stands in for subgroups)
fix: A proposal can advance with discussed objections unresolved, because it advances on consensus calls under the 2:1 norm in subgroups and by the convenor at plenary. Consensus need not imply unanimity.

problem: "SD-4 adopts ISO's definition of consensus, marked by the absence of sustained opposition, but names no step for judging or registering one, nor criteria for an important part of the concerned interests." (32 words) and "Whoever ISO's leadership is for a working group, SD-4's own steps for an objection include the 2:1 norm, Against voters' reasons on request, escalation, and plenary's 3-way poll and national-position question." (31 words)
fix: SD-4 adopts ISO's definition of consensus, marked by no sustained opposition, but names no step for judging or registering one, or criteria for an important part of the concerned interests. Whoever ISO's leadership is for a working group, SD-4's steps for an objection include the 2:1 norm, Against voters' reasons on request, escalation, and plenary's 3-way poll and national-position question.

problem: "too few to stop the 2:1 norm"
fix: When an objection's Against votes are too few to keep the 2:1 norm unmet, the cheapest response keeping it met at that poll is no change or a partial change.

problem: "the changes that would win them over"
fix: SD-4 asks an Against voter to be ready to name the changes that would change their position, or to say that none would.

problem: "an objection's argument outlasts its hearers only in writing"
fix: Outside the protected records, only writing keeps an objection's argument after its hearers leave, such as the objector's paper or an author's paper showing alternatives or defending a declined change.

problem: "an objector who presses on after a consensus call"
fix: SD-4 describes an objector who keeps objecting after a consensus call, without new information or allowed escalation, as not accepting a group decision, whether or not anyone answered it.

problem: "It says the same of a ballot comment repeating an objection decided where its national body was present and heard, unless the comment brings new information or the body warned all along that it would vote No." (37 words)
fix: It describes likewise a ballot comment repeating an objection decided with its national body present and heard, unless it brings new information or the body always warned of a No.

problem: "Every design needs more than merit to be considered: a proposal needs an on-time paper and a presenter, a rival needs a paper to exist, and objections need fixed forms and times." (32 words) and "Participants learn how the committee applies these rules partly by attending, some of it only that way, and other things equal, whoever knows more has the better chance of adoption, whatever their design skill." (34 words)
fix: Every design needs more than merit to be considered: a proposal needs an on-time paper and a presenter, a rival a paper, and objections fixed forms and times. Participants learn how the committee applies them partly, and some only, by attending, and other things equal, whoever knows more has the better chance of adoption, whatever their design skill.

problem: "though SD-4 expects everyone to know its procedures" (the claim holds without the concession)
fix: Other things equal, a newcomer, lacking what earlier meetings teach, spends more effort getting a paper considered than a returning participant, and SD-4 expects everyone to know its procedures.

problem: "A design that passes a direction poll in a design room is the incumbent on its topic until it fails a later direction poll there." (restates d:incumbent)
fix: cut, and cite d:incumbent in p:incumbent-start

problem: "Yet passing it in a design room makes the design the incumbent."
fix: Passing it in a design room makes the design the incumbent.

problem: "Those who have not read a paper or followed its discussion typically abstain, so a proposal costing more to read than most stakes in it is voted on mainly by those with large stakes." (34 words)
fix: Since those who neither read a paper nor followed its discussion typically abstain, those with large stakes cast most votes on a proposal costing more to read than most stakes.

problem: "faces three obstacles at once"
fix: For an objector who arrives after a design has been adopted, three things hold at once.

problem: "Removal needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, reversal costs more for every decision built on the design, and the record keeps its case but unwritten objections only in memory." (33 words)
fix: Removal needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, reversal costs more as more is built, and the record keeps its case but unwritten objections only in memory.

problem: "A first part that fixes a design's structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need of it, and then every rival to that structure must replace it." (33 words) and "SD-4 asks no paper to state those needs, so a design-bound author's best first paper is the smallest part that fixes the structure and still meets the 2:1 norm against opponents who foresee the rest." (35 words)
fix: A first part fixing a design's structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need, and every rival to that structure must then replace it. SD-4 asks no paper to state those needs, so a design-bound author does best with the smallest first part that fixes the structure and passes against opponents foreseeing the rest.

problem: "can keep it below the 2:1 line"
fix: Against votes on the first part can keep it from meeting the 2:1 norm, while removing it once adopted needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the norm.

problem: "A large proposal has more sponsored authors in the room than a small one, and is expected to face more meetings where a poll can make it the incumbent or end its incumbency." (33 words)
fix: A large proposal has more sponsored authors in the room than a small one, and more expected meetings where a poll can make it the incumbent or end its incumbency.

problem: "Each result in this chapter about large or small proposals rests on an attribute their definitions name: who pays the authors' costs, the number of authors, review's expected span, or the paper's length." (33 words)
fix: Each result here about large or small proposals rests on an attribute their definitions name: who pays the authors' costs, how many authors, review's expected span, or paper length.

problem: "puts a sponsor's voters where the design the design room starts from is chosen" (the participants vote in their own right and value its interests among their other values)
fix: Paying participants to attend a study group puts participants who value the sponsor's interests where the design the design room starts from is chosen.

problem: "On a count above 2:1 after discussion, with Neutral votes short of a majority, a design room chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost ranks declaring consensus above declining." (33 words; the chair-call table caption already holds both conditions)
fix: In the case the table below describes, a design room chair ranks declaring consensus above declining on a count above 2:1 after discussion.

problem: "a chair who follows the norm does not declare consensus" and "Declining, after any re-poll, does not depart from it."
fix: On a count at or below 2:1 after discussion, a chair who follows the norm declines, so declaring consensus departs from it. Declining, after any re-poll, fits the norm.

problem: "what departing from SD-4's norm can cost them"
fix: A design room chair's consensus call, when the chair's stake in the proposal is worth less to them than what departing from the 2:1 norm can cost them.

problem: "which promises fewer problems"
fix: Of two papers otherwise alike, a chair does better taking up first the one whose author's record of following procedures and responding to review makes them expect fewer problems.

problem: "Most polls pass by unanimous consent, and when opposition is significant the convenor usually asks" (states practice as fact rather than as what SD-4 says)
fix: SD-4 says most polls pass by unanimous consent, and when opposition is significant the convenor usually asks whether Against votes are personal or national body positions.

problem: "yet only those who bear the cost of taking part"
fix: Fees are barred and everyone in a subgroup's room has one vote, and only those who bear the cost of taking part, or whose sponsors do, vote in WG21's polls.

problem: "participants propose for needs they and their sponsors know" (says what participants do)
fix: ISO can remove inactive national body experts, and participants can propose only for needs they and their sponsors know, which need not match users' needs.

problem: "Authors get the adoption they value at the poll, while a flaw that implementation and use have not yet exposed costs users only later, and can fall on any user of the feature." (33 words)
fix: Authors get the adoption they value at the poll. A flaw that implementation and use have not yet exposed costs users only later, and can fall on any user of the feature.

problem: "Winning a consensus call and producing the design that serves users best coincide only as far as voters can judge that at the poll and no other value they hold outweighs it." (32 words)
fix: Winning a consensus call and producing the design serving users best coincide only as far as voters can judge that at the poll and weigh no other value above it.

problem: "No rule requires a written answer to an objection beyond three: an author's defense of declining a directed change, ISO's response to enquiry ballot comments, and a TS ballot's Disposition of Comments." (32 words) and "For the author, a written answer stating the objection makes it easier to raise again, but also shows later what would not be new, the test SD-4 applies to repeated objections." (31 words)
fix: No rule requires a written answer to an objection beyond an author's defense of declining a directed change, ISO's response to enquiry comments, and a TS ballot's Disposition of Comments. For the author, a written answer stating the objection makes it easier to raise again but also shows later readers what would not be new, SD-4's test for repeated objections.

problem: "So does an Against vote keeping it at or below the 2:1 line."
fix: So does an Against vote that keeps its count from meeting the 2:1 norm.

problem: "It also reaches implementers and users early and can publish while concerns remain, if their holders agree, and the design room can require one, or the lighter white paper ISO and SC22 now recommend." (34 words; "lighter" is also a figure of speech)
fix: It reaches implementers and users early, can publish while concerns remain if their holders agree, and the design room can require it or the white paper ISO and SC22 recommend.

problem: "Every national body may vote on enquiry and final ballots, which pass when two thirds of the P-members' counted votes are positive and at most a quarter of all counted votes negative." (32 words) and "Abstentions and negative votes without technical comments go uncounted, ISO encourages abstaining without national consensus or expert input, sustained opposition does not apply, and a failed final draft returns to SC22." (31 words)
fix: Every national body may vote on enquiry and final ballots, which pass with two thirds of P-members' counted votes positive and at most a quarter of all counted votes negative. Abstentions and negative votes without technical comments go uncounted, ISO encourages abstaining without national consensus or expert input, sustained opposition is inapplicable, and a failed final draft returns to SC22.

problem: "In the cases the table below describes, a body valuing the rest of a document does better voting Yes with comments, and one wanting the work in no form does better voting No." (33 words)
fix: In the table's cases, a body valuing the rest of a document does better voting Yes with comments, and one wanting the work in no form does better voting No.

problem: ""Values the rest" means it values publishing the rest of the document on schedule above removing any one feature through a failed ballot and a revised draft, and expects its comments to fare the same under any vote, as SD-4 says." (41 words)
fix: "Values the rest" means it values publishing the rest of the document on schedule above removing any one feature through a failed ballot and a revised draft. It also expects its comments to fare the same under any vote, as SD-4 says.

problem: "At ballot, a national body whose comments fare the same under any vote does better voting No over one feature only if it values removing that feature above the rest of the document on schedule." (35 words)
fix: A national body whose comments fare the same under any vote does better voting No over one feature only if it values removing it above the rest on schedule.

problem: "In the United States, INCITS gives each voting member one vote, apart from up to four Defense Department votes, bars consultants a voting member funds from voting membership, and binds all delegates to official positions." (35 words)
fix: In the United States, INCITS gives each organization one vote, the Defense Department up to four, no vote to consultants a voting member funds, and binds delegates to official positions.

problem: "INCITS gives each organization one voting membership, apart from up to four Department of Defense votes on technical committees, and treats an entity another controls as part of it on its Executive Board." (33 words) and "It admits a consultant as a voting member only if no voting member funds it, and lets the representatives of standards developing organizations and consortia be employed by other voting members." (31 words)
fix: INCITS gives each organization one voting membership, except up to four Department of Defense votes on technical committees, and on its Executive Board counts a controlled entity with its controller. It admits a consultant as a voting member only if no voting member funds it, and lets standards developing organizations and consortia be represented by other voting members' employees.

problem: "Whatever other moves a regular takes, the votes above still do best for them, since staying out of a poll counts as not voting and the rest go with any vote." (31 words)
fix: Whatever other moves a regular takes, the votes above do best for them, since staying out of a poll counts as not voting and the rest go with any vote.

problem: "Whatever the others choose, a design-bound author does best seeking direction polls as early as they can pass, proposing first the smallest part that fixes its features and can pass, and choosing the IS where it can pass." (38 words) and "It does best leaving out a trade-off no reviewer would raise when stating it now costs more than later exposure would, seeking no poll it expects to lose to a rival, and answering objections with the cheapest change that keeps the design passing." (43 words)
fix: Whatever the others choose, a design-bound author does best seeking direction polls once they can pass and proposing first the smallest part that fixes its features and can pass. It does best choosing the IS where it can pass, and leaving out a trade-off no reviewer would raise when stating it now costs more than later exposure would. It also does best seeking no poll it expects to lose to a rival, and answering objections with the cheapest change that keeps the design passing.

problem: "Declining a change the room directs harms the proposal's chances" ("harms" sits outside the quotation)
fix: Declining a change the room directs lowers the proposal's chances, SD-4 says, and it asks an author who declines to defend that decision and bring new information.

problem: "It does best seeking an early poll or first part only where sooner adoption outweighs the cost it adds to later improvements, and backing any rival that serves users better by more than its share of the reversal's cost." (39 words)
fix: It does best seeking an early poll or first part only where sooner adoption outweighs the cost it adds to later improvements. It does best backing any rival that serves users better by more than its share of the reversal's cost.

problem: "Every later change to an incumbent, or to a design built on adopted parts, must redo or discard work built on it, at a cost that grows as more is built." (31 words)
fix: Every later change to an incumbent, or to a design built on adopted parts, must redo or discard work built on it, at a cost growing as more is built.

problem: "When one option is better for users and in the features, or the options differ in only one of these, an author who values both does best taking the better option." (31 words)
fix: When one option is better for users and in the features, or the options differ in only one, an author who values both does best taking the better one.

problem: "Stating it would lead the room to change, in a way that serves users better, a feature a design-bound author's gain depends on, and the proposal meets the 2:1 norm either way." (32 words)
fix: Stating it would lead the room to change a feature a design-bound author's gain depends on, in a way that serves users better. The proposal meets the 2:1 norm either way.

problem: "Whatever the others choose, a small proposal's author does best keeping it presented while its chance of adoption is worth more to them than the cost, borne alone, of the meetings still ahead." (33 words)
fix: Whatever the others choose, a small proposal's author does best keeping it presented while its chance of adoption outweighs the cost, borne alone, of the meetings still ahead.

problem: "A chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them does better making the call that norm gives: a design that meets it, or none when none does." (31 words)
fix: A chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them does better making the call that norm gives: a design meeting it, or none when none does.

problem: "A chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them does better making the call the norm gives, which here sends on a design that meets it, or none." (32 words)
fix: A chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them does better making the call the norm gives, which sends on a design meeting it, or none.

problem: "that is consensus above the line and declining at or below it"
fix: With Neutral votes short of a majority, that is consensus on a count above 2:1 and declining on any other, after any re-poll.

problem: "since it promises fewer problems"
fix: Of two papers otherwise alike, a design room chair does better taking up first the one whose author's record of following the procedures makes them expect fewer problems.

problem: "A one-meeting delay for a paperless rival postpones the poll without changing how its count is called, and at the feature cutoff it sends the proposal to the next planned edition." (31 words)
fix: A one-meeting delay for a paperless rival postpones the poll without changing how its count is called, and at the feature cutoff sends the proposal to the next planned edition.

problem: "That procedure fixes the call in two cases, declaring consensus when no one objects to unanimous consent or when all opposition is unescalated and holds no national position, and otherwise leaves it to the convenor." (35 words)
fix: That procedure has the convenor declare consensus when nobody objects to unanimous consent or all opposition is unescalated and holds no national position, and otherwise leaves the call to them.

problem: "Whatever the others choose, a national body whose comments fare the same under any vote does best voting Yes with comments if it values a document's rest above removing any one feature, and No otherwise." (35 words)
fix: Whatever the others choose, a national body whose comments fare alike under every vote does best voting Yes with comments if it values the document's rest above removing any feature. Otherwise it does best voting No. (The item's last sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "A national body whose comments fare the same under any vote, and which values removing some one feature at least as much as the rest of the document, does best voting No." (32 words)
fix: A national body whose comments fare alike under every vote, and which values removing some one feature at least as much as the document's rest, does best voting No.

problem: "Whatever the others choose, a sponsor does best paying for participants in the rooms whose decisions it values, study groups included, while what their votes bring it is worth their cost." (31 words; "the rooms" also stands in for subgroups)
fix: Whatever the others choose, a sponsor does best paying for participants in the subgroups whose decisions it values, study groups included, while their votes bring it at least their cost.

problem: "Whatever the others choose, a user without a sponsor does best taking part only when their own stake outweighs the full price, which they bear alone while any better design's gain goes to all users." (35 words)
fix: Whatever the others choose, a user without a sponsor does best taking part only when their own stake outweighs the full price, which they bear alone. Any better design's gain goes to all users. (The item's last sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "Plenary invites serious design concerns, national bodies vote on each balloted draft and get answers to enquiry comments, editing committees verify applied changes, minutes can be challenged, and national bodies can appeal." (32 words)
fix: Plenary invites serious design concerns, national bodies vote on each balloted draft, get answers to enquiry comments, and can appeal, editing committees verify applied changes, and minutes can be challenged.

problem: "Chairs may allow limited exploration of alternatives, and SD-4 encourages polling alternatives side by side and asks a good paper to show the alternatives considered, its design principles, and motivating examples from today's code." (34 words)
fix: Chairs may allow limited exploration of alternatives, and SD-4 encourages side-by-side polls and asks a good paper for alternatives considered, design principles, and motivating examples from today's code.

problem: "SD-4 asks those with a concern to tell chairs and authors early, ... and editing committees verify applied changes." (39 words) and "Minutes can be challenged, national bodies can appeal, ... and SD-4 works in addition to the Directives." (46 words)
fix: SD-4 asks those with a concern to tell chairs and authors early, plenary solicits serious design concerns, and national bodies vote on each enquiry and final ballot. Every enquiry comment gets a written response, editing committees verify applied changes, and minutes can be challenged. National bodies can appeal, on drafts only over principle or harm to ISO's or IEC's reputation, and ISO says consensus requires resolving substantial objections. ISO ends the committee stage when all technical issues are resolved, and SD-4 works in addition to the Directives.

problem: "A design-bound author seeks direction polls as early as they can pass, proposes first the smallest part that fixes the features it needs and can pass, and chooses the IS where it can pass." (34 words)
fix: A design-bound author seeks early direction polls, proposes first the smallest part fixing the features it needs, and chooses the IS, each as far as it can pass.

problem: "A national body whose comments fare the same under any vote votes Yes with comments unless removing one feature is worth as much to it as the rest of the document." (31 words)
fix: A national body whose comments fare alike under any vote votes Yes with comments unless removing one feature is worth as much to it as the rest of the document.

problem: "An objector who arrives after adoption needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, faces a reversal cost that has grown, and finds unwritten objections kept only in memory." (31 words)
fix: An objector arriving after adoption needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, faces a reversal cost that has grown, and finds unwritten objections kept only in memory.

problem: "No SD-4 step checks whether separately adopted designs work together, review worth its cost to users together but not to any one participant goes undone, and the record need not show whether objections were answered." (35 words)
fix: No SD-4 step checks whether separately adopted designs work together, and review worth its cost to users together but not to any one participant goes undone. The record need not show whether objections were answered.

problem: "A first part that fixes a structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need of it, and every rival to that structure must then replace it." (32 words)
fix: A first part fixing a structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need, and every rival to that structure must then replace it.

problem: "The rules also provide checks: a third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, every view must be heard, rivals with papers can be polled together, implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies ballot each draft." (35 words)
fix: The rules also provide checks: a third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, and every view must be heard. Rivals with papers can be polled together, implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies ballot each draft.

problem: "a poll has placed it among the work aimed at the next IS"
fix: The same holds when the chair expects fewer problems from it, a poll has placed it among the work aimed at the next edition, or it is already the incumbent.

problem: "A choice doing at least as well as any other, given the others' choices, leaves its player nothing to gain by changing only that choice." (restates d:settled-pattern)
fix: cut, and cite d:settled-pattern in l:thm-pattern

problem: "From then on, every rival and every later change must redo or discard work built on the design, at a cost that grows as more is built, whether or not it is wrong." (33 words)
fix: Thereafter, every rival and later change must redo or discard work built on the design, at a cost growing as more is built, whether or not it is wrong.

problem: "An objector who arrives after adoption needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, faces a reversal cost that has grown, and finds unwritten objections kept only in memory." (31 words)
fix: An objector arriving after adoption needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, faces a reversal cost that has grown, and finds unwritten objections kept only in memory.

problem: "a poll has placed it among the work aimed at the next IS"
fix: The same holds when the chair expects fewer problems from it, a poll has placed it among the work aimed at the next edition, or it is already the incumbent.

problem: "among the work aimed at the next IS"
fix: A poll placing a proposal among the work aimed at the next edition puts it in a category SD-4 has chairs take up first.

problem: "Participants propose for needs they and their sponsors know" (says what participants do)
fix: Participants can propose only for needs they and their sponsors know, which need not match users' needs, since users differ from them in what matters.

problem: "Each participant a sponsor pays to attend has a vote, and no rule limits how many it pays, though SC22 may cap how many experts each national body or liaison appoints." (31 words; "though" also concedes where the claim holds without it)
fix: Each participant a sponsor pays to attend has a vote, and no rule limits how many it pays, while SC22 may cap the experts each national body or liaison appoints.

problem: "Winning a consensus call and producing the design that serves users best coincide only as far as voters can judge that at the poll and no other value they hold outweighs it." (32 words)
fix: Winning a consensus call and producing the design serving users best coincide only as far as voters can judge that at the poll and weigh no other value above it.

problem: "No SD-4 step checks whether separately adopted designs work together, review worth its cost to users together but not to any one participant goes undone, and the record need not show whether objections were answered." (35 words)
fix: No SD-4 step checks whether separately adopted designs work together, and review worth its cost to users together but not to any one participant goes undone. The record need not show whether objections were answered.

problem: "A first part that fixes a structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need of it, and every rival to that structure must then replace it." (32 words)
fix: A first part fixing a structure can be adopted before reviewers can study in detail what later parts need, and every rival to that structure must then replace it.

problem: "The rules also provide checks: a third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, every view must be heard, rivals with papers can be polled together, implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies ballot each draft." (35 words)
fix: The rules also provide checks: a third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, and every view must be heard. Rivals with papers can be polled together, implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies ballot each draft. (The item's last sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "A third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, every view must be heard, rivals with papers can be polled together, implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies vote on each balloted draft." (32 words)
fix: A third of the Favor-plus-Against votes can block, every view must be heard, and rivals with papers can be polled together. Implementation experience informs votes, and national bodies vote on each balloted draft.

problem: "SD-4 keeps records of subgroup discussion password-protected but lets poll questions and numeric results be quoted, and each prediction names its evidence, counter-evidence, another explanation, and the data telling them apart." (31 words)
fix: SD-4 password-protects records of subgroup discussion but lets poll questions and numeric results be quoted, and each prediction names its evidence, counter-evidence, another explanation, and the data telling them apart.

problem: "Where one sponsor pays a proposal's authors and many participants present, ... poll results and stated affiliations are the evidence." (37 words) and "No smaller share would count against it, and comparing, by consented attribution, ... would tell it apart from shared technical views." (39 words)
fix: Where one sponsor pays a proposal's authors and many participants present, and its interests include adoption, the model predicts a smaller Against share of the Favor-plus-Against votes than elsewhere. Poll results and stated affiliations are the evidence, and no smaller share would count against it. Comparing, by consented attribution, participants' votes on its proposals before and after they move to a sponsor whose interests exclude them would tell it apart from shared technical views.

problem: "so the more of those present it pays, the smaller the Against share of the Favor-plus-Against votes" (states the predicted result as fact)
fix: Each participant the sponsor pays has a vote and values its interests, so the model predicts that the more of those present it pays, the smaller the Against share. (The second sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "Among proposals with similar stakes polled in one room at one meeting, the model predicts fewer votes cast the longer the paper; quotable poll results and paper lengths are the evidence." (31 words) and "No fall would count against it, and comparing papers on topics of similar breadth but different length would tell it apart from another explanation, that longer papers cover narrower topics fewer participants know." (33 words)
fix: Among proposals with similar stakes polled in one room at one meeting, the model predicts fewer votes the longer the paper; quotable poll results and paper lengths are the evidence. No fall would count against it. Comparing papers of different length on equally broad topics would tell it apart from another explanation, that longer papers cover narrower topics fewer participants know.

problem: "so in one room at one meeting, longer papers with similar stakes draw fewer votes" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: Participants who did not study a paper typically skip its polls, so the model predicts fewer votes on longer papers with similar stakes in one room at one meeting. (The second sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "The model predicts that large proposals tend to arrive as sequences of papers, ... and large designs mostly adopted in one paper would count against it." (36 words) and "Another explanation is that large designs are easier to review in parts; ... would tell them apart." (37 words)
fix: The model predicts that large proposals tend to arrive as sequences of papers, each building on adopted parts; the mailings are the evidence. Large designs mostly adopted in one paper would count against it, and another explanation is that large designs are easier to review in parts. Whether later parts already drafted or implemented when the first was polled stayed out of the mailings until it was adopted would tell them apart.

problem: "The model predicts that first papers of designs later extended part by part describe a small scope and seldom set out the later parts; the mailings are the evidence, and first papers setting them out would count against it." (39 words)
fix: The model predicts that first papers of designs later extended part by part describe a small scope and seldom set out the later parts; the mailings are the evidence. First papers setting them out would count against it, and another explanation is that small first steps lower risk. Whether first papers left out later parts that already existed in drafts, implementations, or talks would tell them apart.

problem: "So first papers of designs extended part by part seldom set out their later parts" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: So the model predicts that first papers of designs extended part by part seldom set out their later parts, and first papers setting them out would count against it.

problem: "The model predicts that once a design passes a design room's direction poll, a like rival draws less support than before in polls of the same form; quotable poll results are the evidence, and equal support would count against it." (40 words)
fix: The model predicts that once a design passes a design room's direction poll, a like rival draws less support than before in polls of the same form. Quotable poll results are the evidence, and equal support would count against it. (The item's last sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "The model predicts rare removals after adoption, ... working drafts, ballot comments, and poll results are the evidence." (36 words) and "Frequent removals by narrow margins would count against it, ... that adopted designs rarely need removal." (33 words)
fix: The model predicts rare removals after adoption, by paper or ballot comment, likelier when national bodies whose No votes could fail a ballot oppose the design. Working drafts, ballot comments, and poll results are the evidence, and frequent removals by narrow margins would count against it. Comparing removals with the papers or comments asking for them would tell it apart from another explanation, that adopted designs rarely need removal.

problem: "So removals are rare" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: So the model predicts rare removals, and frequent removals by narrow margins would count against the prediction.

problem: "so removal is then more likely" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: When national bodies whose No votes could fail a ballot oppose a design, keeping it risks the whole document, a cost removal avoids. So the model predicts removal is then more likely.

problem: "The model predicts that small proposals stop advancing without a negative poll more often than large ones; the mailings and poll results are the evidence, and no such difference would count against it." (33 words)
fix: The model predicts that small proposals stop advancing without a negative poll more often than large ones; the mailings and poll results are the evidence. No such difference would count against it, and another explanation is that small proposals are more often dropped on reflection. Comparing stops by self-funded and sponsored authors on papers of similar length would tell them apart.

problem: "So small proposals stop advancing without a negative poll more often than large ones" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: Sponsors pay a large proposal's authors' costs, while a small proposal's author pays their own. So the model predicts that small proposals stop advancing without a negative poll more often than large ones, and no such difference would count against it.

problem: "The model predicts that national bodies state positions on few proposals; vetted national body comments and plenary records of national positions are the evidence, and positions on most proposals would count against it." (33 words)
fix: The model predicts that national bodies state positions on few proposals; vetted national body comments and plenary records of national positions are the evidence. Positions on most proposals would count against it, and another explanation is that national bodies agree with most proposals. Comparing how often they state positions on proposals with and without Against votes in subgroups would tell them apart.

problem: "The model predicts that papers advancing over Against votes often leave unstated the objections other published papers raised against them; the papers and poll results are the evidence, and routine answers would count against it." (35 words)
fix: The model predicts that papers advancing over Against votes often leave unstated the objections other published papers raised against them; the papers and poll results are the evidence. Routine answers would count against it, and another explanation is that the objections were answered in discussion. Comparing such papers with what subgroup chairs answer at plenary when an objection is raised there would tell them apart.

problem: "If some unresolved objections point to real defects, the model predicts more defects found after adoption in features a design room forwarded over Against votes than in those forwarded with none; issues lists, correction papers, removals, and poll results are the evidence." (42 words)
fix: If some unresolved objections point to real defects, the model predicts more post-adoption defects in features a design room forwarded over Against votes than in those forwarded with none. Issues lists, correction papers, removals, and poll results are the evidence, and no difference would count against it. Comparing features matched on scope, novelty, prior implementation, and use would tell it apart from another explanation, that contested features draw more scrutiny.

problem: "features a design room forwarded over Against votes show more defects found after adoption than those forwarded with none" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: So if some unresolved objections point to real defects, the model predicts more post-adoption defects in features a design room forwarded over Against votes than in those forwarded with none. (The second sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "If closer study finds more defects, the model predicts fewer defects after adoption on topics ... author lists, mailings, issues lists, and removals are the evidence." (39 words) and "No difference would count against it, and comparing topics of equal novelty and poll turnout would tell it apart from another explanation, that important or well-understood topics draw rival papers and attention anyway." (33 words)
fix: If closer study finds more defects, the model predicts fewer post-adoption defects on topics whose deciding poll had competing papers from separate author groups than on one-paper topics. Author lists, mailings, issues lists, and removals are the evidence, and no difference would count against it. Comparing topics of equal novelty and poll turnout would tell it apart from another explanation, that important or well-understood topics draw rival papers and attention anyway.

problem: "topics whose deciding poll had competing papers from separate author groups show fewer defects after adoption than one-paper topics" (states the prediction as fact)
fix: So if closer study finds more defects, the model predicts fewer post-adoption defects on topics whose deciding poll had competing papers from separate author groups than on one-paper topics. (The second sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "If SD-4 asked voters of every position to be ready to give reasons when the chair asks, Neutral would bear the reasons cost Against now bears, while not voting would bear none." (32 words)
fix: If SD-4 asked voters of every position to be ready to give reasons on request, Neutral would bear the reasons cost Against now bears, while not voting would bear none.

problem: "how many participants one sponsor pays may vote in a room" ("a room" stands in for a subgroup)
fix: If the rules limited how many participants one sponsor pays may vote in a subgroup, the votes cast there by participants valuing its interests would be capped.

problem: "limiting how many of them may vote in a room" ("a room" stands in for a subgroup)
fix: Each participant a sponsor pays to attend has a vote and values its interests, so limiting how many of them may vote in a subgroup caps those votes.

problem: "If forming national positions during meetings cost less, national bodies would take more, and more plenary opposition would hold national positions, whose weight SD-4's procedure leaves to the convenor rather than the count." (33 words)
fix: If forming national positions during meetings cost less, national bodies would take more, and more plenary opposition would hold them. SD-4's procedure leaves the weight of such opposition to the convenor rather than the count. (The item's last sentence follows unchanged.)

problem: "If forming national positions during meetings cost more, ... the ballot vote would be their only move counting directly toward stopping a document." (35 words) and "Comments and appeals would remain, ... and the model predicts attendance, paid participants, and early incumbency deciding more content." (31 words)
fix: If forming national positions during meetings cost more, national bodies would take fewer, and plenary would seldom meet opposition holding them. Their ballot vote would be their only move counting directly toward stopping a document. Comments and appeals would remain, appeals on drafts only for principle or harm to ISO's or IEC's reputation. The model predicts attendance, paid participants, and early incumbency deciding more content.

problem: Its "three or more" and "two more than before" need the threshold without that vote, which only its sibling inf:met-without-vote (or f:two-to-one with d:positions) supplies; l:against-double gives only the shift of two.
fix: Add inf:met-without-vote to the basis.

problem: The ISO half of "need not show whether an objection was answered or outvoted" rests on no cited item: f:iso-no-reason-record covers only why consensus was judged to exist, and l:record-checks and l:iso-register-level state no absence.
fix: Add f:iso-no-answer to the basis, which states that the searched clauses require no written answer to an objection raised in a working group.

problem: "Removing or replacing an adopted design is a reversal" rests on d:reversal, which it does not cite, and neither ind:reversal-grows nor p:challenger-bar classifies the removal of an adopted design.
fix: Add d:reversal to the basis.

problem: "Each part needs its own paper" rests on no cited item: ax:review-cost, f:present-required, and the forwarding facts say nothing about a paper being required.
fix: Add f:no-paper (or inf:part-is-addition) to the basis.

problem: Ranking No strictly above abstaining needs the table's premise that the body cannot rule out its vote deciding the result, which l:rank-rest-yes builds in through "as the table below defines it" and inf:comments-either-way, but this lemma and inf:oppose-no-rank omit, and l:rank-oppose-abstain's "such a body" inherits the gap.
fix: Scope the lemma to a body that wants the work in no form "as the table below defines it", which carries to l:rank-oppose-abstain.

problem: Under d:rules, "no step the rules require" covers SD-4 whole and the quoted ISO clauses, but its only absence basis, f:no-drawbacks-asked, searched SD-4 alone.
fix: Extend f:no-drawbacks-asked's search to the ISO clauses d:rules names, as f:no-sponsor-cap does, which also repairs p:same-moves, l:thm-disclosure, inf:thm-no-request, inf:thm-omit-free, and the Theorem; failing that, say "SD-4" in place of "the rules".

problem: "The author cannot rule out losing standing" rests on no cited item: ax:prefer and d:standing say only that the author values standing, and ax:support gives a standing risk only for an Against vote.
fix: Cite a premise that gives this risk, which no axiom now does, or drop the clause, since l:bound-omit's comparison holds without it.

problem: It says "the rules" ask no statement of drawbacks, a sponsor, or what the author's gain depends on, but f:no-drawbacks-asked and f:no-interest-statement searched SD-4 alone, while d:rules makes such a claim cover the quoted ISO clauses too.
fix: Extend both facts' searches to the ISO clauses d:rules names, or say "SD-4" in place of "the rules".

problem: Its first sentence says every study group chair does best polling and following the 2:1 norm, but l:sg-call, l:sg-side-by-side, and l:sg-other-moves prove this only for a chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them.
fix: Narrow the first sentence's subject to that chair, as l:settled-design-chair does, and keep the second sentence.

problem: inf:nb-early-cost shows only that a change won early costs those who built on the design less, and nothing cited makes a cheaper change likelier to be made, which is what would make raising an objection early better for the national body than raising it later but still in time.
fix: Add a premise that a cheaper change wins voters more readily, such as p:challenger-bar's weighing of each voter's share of the cost.

problem: "The rules ask no author to state their own design's drawbacks" and "no step the rules require before adoption" are claims about SD-4 and the quoted ISO clauses, but through l:thm-disclosure they rest on f:no-drawbacks-asked, which searched SD-4 alone.
fix: Apply the fix given for inf:omit-free, or say "SD-4" in both places.

problem: The children show that each named choice does best whatever else its player does, but the Theorem leaves some choices open, such as a result-seeking author's vehicle request (p:prefer-is shows the vehicles differ for it), a chair's one-meeting delay at the feature cutoff, and the convenor's call where SD-4 leaves it open, so a player could still gain by changing one of those.
fix: State once, in the Theorem or here, that in the pattern each player also makes every choice the Theorem leaves open in whichever way does best for them given the others' choices, which inf:thm-other-moves shows leaves the named choices best.

problem: That objectors short of a third leave the 2:1 norm met is the converse of what l:vote-count states (at least a third keeps it unmet), and only l:under-third states that converse.
fix: Add l:under-third to the basis.

problem: "A change to a design costs the sponsors who have built on it" covers any change, but its only basis, inf:thm-change-cost, covers changes to the features a sponsor's interests depend on.
fix: Add ax:rework, under which any change made after work is built on a design costs those who built it.

problem: "In this pattern no participant does it" needs the pattern to fix each participant's choice whether to study, but no named choice covers studying, which inf:regular-alongside treats as a move that goes with any vote.
fix: The scope statement proposed for l:thm-pattern makes this step follow.

problem: Its claims that the rules ask no author to state drawbacks and require no step before adoption rest on f:no-drawbacks-asked, which searched SD-4 alone, while d:rules makes such claims cover the quoted ISO clauses too.
fix: Apply the fix given for inf:omit-free.

problem: "Ask no author to state their own design's drawbacks" is claimed for the rules but rests on p:same-moves and f:no-drawbacks-asked, whose search covered SD-4 alone.
fix: Apply the fix given for inf:omit-free.

problem: "No step the rules require before adoption" rests through inf:omit-free on f:no-drawbacks-asked, which searched SD-4 alone.
fix: Apply the fix given for inf:omit-free.

problem: inf:al-study gives fewer participants for whom close study is worth its time, but f:not-vote makes abstention typical only for those who did not read the paper or follow the discussion, so the step to fewer votes treats skipping close study as skipping reading.
fix: Base the step on l:skip-study, under which a longer paper's higher reading cost leaves fewer readers among those with similar stakes, or say "read" in place of "close study" in inf:al-study.

problem: "Which publishing them forgoes" assumes reviewers can study a later part once its paper is in the mailings, but ax:first-review, the cited source of the gain, says they cannot study it in detail until that part is presented.
fix: State once, in ax:first-review or here, that reviewers can study a later part in detail once its paper is in the mailings, or else predict that later parts go unpresented rather than unpublished.

problem: Both clauses, a small scope and seldom setting out the later parts, are claimed for all first papers of designs extended part by part, but inf:fp-small and inf:fp-seldom derive them only from design-bound authors' choices, and nothing cited makes a result-seeking author leave the later parts out.
fix: Narrow the subject to designs by design-bound authors, or add a cited premise that design-bound authors write most designs extended part by part.

problem: It extends to all first papers of designs extended part by part a choice that inf:fp-small and l:settled-design-bound give only design-bound authors, while l:settled-result-seeking has a result-seeking author state what improves the design whenever that outweighs the votes it costs.
fix: Narrow the subject to designs by design-bound authors, or add a cited premise that design-bound authors write most designs extended part by part.

problem: It states what the model predicts but cites neither inf:fp-seldom nor thm:settled, the items that make it a prediction of the model.
fix: Add inf:fp-seldom to the basis.

problem: The other explanation predicts few requests wherever removals are few only if requests for removal arise mainly where removal is needed, which no cited item supplies (inf:rm-need says only that removals would be rare), and without it many requests with few removals fit both explanations.
fix: Compare removals with requests that later evidence bears out, such as issues lists or correction papers on the same feature, or add a cited premise that requests track need.

problem: Matching on scope, novelty, prior implementation, and use holds fixed only the scrutiny those features bring, but c:pred-defects states the other explanation as contested features drawing more scrutiny, and objectors' own stake in finding defects, the reasoning of inf:co-stake, would survive the matching.
fix: State the other explanation as scrutiny that novelty or use brings, as inf:de-scrutiny does, or also match on a measure of the scrutiny each feature drew.

problem: "Answering it takes more than the cheapest change keeping the 2:1 norm met" needs national-body opposition to be able to stop the proposal, but l:settled-convenor leaves the convenor's call open there, and p:credible-threat makes a No credible only from a body valuing the feature's removal above the rest of the document.
fix: Narrow the subject to objections backed by national bodies whose No votes could fail a ballot, as c:pred-removals does, where inf:later-stages then requires the larger change.

problem: "Plenary would seldom meet opposition holding them" is stronger than its basis, inf:nl-fewer, which gives only less such opposition.
fix: Add inf:nb-few, under which national bodies already state positions on few proposals, so that fewer still makes such opposition seldom.

problem: "The cheapest change a design-bound author then needs to keep it passing in the room is none" leaves out a change the room directs. A poll directing a change can pass with Favor votes beyond the objectors', and SD-4 says a proposal that does not implement design subgroup direction harms its own chances, as l:bound-cheapest itself states. So the Theorem's "can be fixed when it is least reviewed" holds only when the room directs no change.
fix: Add the scope l:bound-cheapest already uses: "The cheapest change a design-bound author then needs to keep it passing in the room is none, unless the room directs one," and cite f:direction-implement.

problem: It treats choosing the polls as a move that comes before the call and so leaves the norm's call best, but l:sg-side-by-side shows that the order of polls can change which design leaves a room, and a design room also polls rivals that have papers (l:rival-with-paper). The pattern names a study group chair's choice of polls but no design room chair's, so l:settled-design-chair and inf:thm-other-moves do not show that a design room chair's choice of polls does best.
fix: Add a child under l:settled-design-chair, parallel to l:sg-side-by-side and resting on f:multiple-polls and ax:post-risk, showing that a design room chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost does best polling competing designs side by side, and name that choice in the Theorem.

problem: "so in this pattern no participant does it" needs the pattern to include a choice about studying, but the Theorem names none, and inf:regular-alongside treats studying as a move that goes with any vote. As built, the pattern says nothing about study, so the conclusion that such review goes undone does not follow from l:thm-pattern.
fix: Name the study choice in l:settled-regular and the Theorem, from l:study-worth and l:skip-study: a participant studies a paper only when what studying brings them through the poll is worth the time. Then cite that choice here.

problem: Check the proof does not state: SD-4 asks design room discussion to "help achieve a broad understanding of the proposal within the design subgroup," which works against a proposal being voted on mainly by those with large stakes.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the whole sentence word for word, "Discussion should be constructive, help achieve a broad understanding of the proposal within the design subgroup, and to result in polls that give the proposal author meaningful and actionable feedback on whether and how to improve the proposal." (SD-4, "Subgroup responsibility and polls"), and list it among the checks in l:checks-hearing. p:light-review can stand as written.

problem: "Asking Against voters for reasons requires knowing who they are, so anonymity ends those requests" is false as written: a chair can still invite whoever voted Against to give reasons without knowing who they are. What anonymity ends is a request to a particular voter.
fix: Weaker wording, since the sentence is false as written: "Anonymity ends the chair's requests to particular Against voters, so giving reasons becomes each voter's own choice, and with it the time an Against vote takes in preparing reasons." The prediction in c:lever-anonymous is unchanged.

problem: "the other explanation predicts few such requests wherever removals are few" is unsupported. Requests for removal come from anyone who wants a design removed, including those outvoted when it was adopted, as SD-4's rule on repeated ballot comments shows (f:ballot-decided), whether or not the design needs removal. Few needed removals then do not imply few requests, and where requests are many both explanations predict rare removals, so the comparison does not separate them.
fix: Narrower subject: compare removals with the requests that bring new information (f:ballot-new-info). There the other explanation predicts few such requests, while the model predicts rare removals even where such requests are many.

problem: SD-4 asks the subgroup chair "to answer whether that item was considered and to summarize the result of the discussion and the reason for the decision of the subgroup." A summary that the room considered an objection and decided otherwise does not show whether it was answered or outvoted, which p:record-indistinct says the record need not show. So the chair's summary cannot sort answered objections from outvoted ones.
fix: Narrower subject: count as favoring the other explanation only summaries that state an answer to the objection's argument, count "considered and decided otherwise" as favoring neither, and cite p:record-indistinct.

problem: It covers the convenor's other moves as appointments, study groups, and guest invitations, but SD-4 gives the convenor another move in plenary: "The Convener may take any polls they choose." No Fact quotes it and m:moves lists no such move, so neither this lemma nor inf:thm-other-moves shows that following SD-4's plenary procedure still does best whatever polls the convenor takes, and the settled pattern is unproved for the convenor.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the whole sentence, "The Convener may take any polls they choose; however, typically the most frequent polls are “3-way” polls where the choices are Favor, Against, and Neutral." (SD-4, "Closing plenary session responsibility and polls"), add the move to the convenor's moves under m:moves, and add to this lemma, as inf:dchair-before-call does for design room chairs, that choosing the polls comes before the call the procedure governs.

problem: "no user votes in any WG21 poll" covers plenary polls, but the only voting rule it cites, f:one-vote, governs subgroup polls. SD-4 states a separate rule for plenary, "In plenary polls, each person present whose nameis listed in the ISO LiveLink global directory can vote," which no Fact quotes. So the claim is unsupported for plenary, and l:traced-voters and p:users-out inherit the gap.
fix: Add a Fact quoting that sentence word for word, misspelling included (SD-4, "Closing plenary session responsibility and polls"), and derive from it and f:registered that each plenary voter is a registered expert, so no user votes there.

problem: SD-4 says "Objections that are not so escalated, but are raised or re-raised in plenary, should not be given weight in plenary," but it does not say that Against votes cast in the 3-way poll it prescribes get no weight, and it leaves the determination of consensus to the convenor. Its next step treats significant Against votes as opposition to classify as personal or national, not as objections to set aside. So "SD-4's plenary procedure has the convenor declare consensus" goes beyond the text, and l:settled-convenor's "fixes the call in two cases" and inf:nm-unsettled rest on it.
fix: Narrower subject: "When all opposition rests on objections not escalated in time and holds no national position, SD-4 says those objections should not be given weight in plenary, so a convenor following SD-4 has no weighted objection to set against consensus." Then restate l:settled-convenor as fixing the call when no one objects to unanimous consent, and as saying otherwise only which objections get no weight.

problem: "the count of those present weighs more in the convenor's call" has no support. d:follows-norm defines how a chair calls consensus on a count, but no item says how the convenor's call depends on the count once opposition has weight, and l:settled-convenor says only that the procedure then leaves the call to the convenor. So the prediction in c:lever-nb-less that paid participants decide more content rests on an unstated premise.
fix: Add the premise once, as a definition parallel to d:follows-norm for the convenor's call when opposition has weight, or narrow the claim to what the proof shows: with fewer national positions, less plenary opposition signals a possible No at ballot.

problem: "less weight at plenary for how many participants each side has present" rests on the same unstated premise as inf:nl-count, since no item says that the count weighs in the convenor's call at all. INCITS's one voting membership per organization governs how the United States position forms, not how the convenor calls consensus.
fix: Add the premise once, as for inf:nl-count, or narrow the claim to "more plenary opposition would hold national positions, formed under each body's own rules, such as INCITS's one voting membership per organization."

problem: Check the proof does not state: ISO tells national bodies that "substantial comments tabled at meetings are counter-productive since no opportunity is available for other delegations to carry out the necessary consultations at home." That limits how far a cheaper national position formed during a meeting turns into more plenary opposition holding one.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the whole sentence word for word, "Moreover, National Bodies need to recognize that substantial comments tabled at meetings are counter-productive since no opportunity is available for other delegations to carry out the necessary consultations at home, without which rapid achievement of consensus will be difficult." (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 0.7), say that it is stated for committee meetings, and name it in c:lever-nb-more.

problem: "plenary records of national positions" are not shown to be usable as evidence. SD-4 keeps meeting wikis password-protected and allows quoting from them only poll questions, numeric results, and words a person consents to have attributed, and a national position is none of these. No cited fact makes plenary records of national positions public or quotable.
fix: Add a cited fact that makes plenary records of national positions public or quotable, or narrow the evidence to sources a cited rule makes available.

problem: Check the proof does not state: ISO says "Meetings should, as a general rule, be organized in locations where entry restrictions or other constraints do not significantly limit the ability of participants to attend." Alongside the fee ban and remote participation, this limits how far the constraints of attending decide who votes.
fix: Add the sentence to f:iso-meetings as a quoted Fact (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 5.3.1), and name it with the fee ban in this proposition.

problem: "choosing the IS where it can pass" has no child that proves it. Its only support, p:prefer-is, names a TS gain open to any author, reaching implementers and users early and publishing while concerns remain, and the lemma never weighs that gain against the TS's delay and its risk to fixed features. A design-bound author can value that earlier reach more than the delay costs, so the "whatever the others choose" claim and the Theorem's matching clause are unproved.
fix: Add a child lemma that weighs a TS's earlier reach against its delay and the risk of incompatible changes, and state its case once, for example "when sooner IS adoption and keeping its features fixed are worth more to it than a TS's earlier reach to implementers and users."

problem: "Votes that follow shared technical views do not depend on who pays the voter, so they would stay the same after the move" is false as written. What a participant learns can change their vote (ax:attention), and proposals change between revisions, so votes can change after a move for reasons unrelated to the new sponsor. A before-and-after comparison alone cannot assign the change to the sponsor.
fix: Narrower subject: compare the movers' change in votes with that of participants who did not move, on the same proposals at the same polls, which holds learning and revisions fixed.

problem: "Reviewing in parts is as easy when later parts already drafted or implemented are in the mailings before the first is adopted" is unsupported.
